title: Read your game's own web traffic
summary: See the HTTP and HTTPS requests your own game sends from your own machine: which servers it calls, what it sends and what comes back. A local proxy; nothing is redirected by force and nothing needs administrator rights.

steps.title: Start mitmproxy from ViWo
steps.text: In RUNTIME, DEBUGGER AND MEMORY: LIST TARGETS, then CONTINUE IN MITMPROXY on the game's executable (CLI: viwo attach <game> --target <key> --tool mitmproxy-gui --workspace <ws> --confirm). The activity console says the proxy address (127.0.0.1 and a port) and where the flows are saved in the workspace.
steps.expect: mitmproxy's window opens in your browser with an empty flow list.

steps.title: Point the game at the proxy
steps.text: Many games follow the system proxy: Windows Settings, Network and internet, Proxy, Manual proxy setup, Use a proxy server, with the address 127.0.0.1 and the port ViWo named. Some games ignore the system proxy; those show nothing here. Turn the system proxy off again when you are done.
steps.expect: Plain HTTP requests of the game, and of every other program on the machine, appear in the list.

steps.title: Decide about HTTPS
steps.text: HTTPS is encrypted: mitmproxy can only show it if you trust its certificate authority on your own machine. That is your choice. With the proxy set, open http://mitm.it in a browser and follow the page for your system; installing for the current user needs no administrator rights. Remove the certificate again when you are done: anyone holding its key could read your traffic.
steps.expect: HTTPS flows show their content. A game that pins its own certificates refuses the connection instead: that traffic cannot be read this way.

steps.title: Find the game's requests
steps.text: Type in the Search field above the list to filter, for example ~d example.com for one domain or ~m POST for one method. Click a flow: Request shows what the game sent, Response what came back.
steps.expect: The flow's headers and body, with JSON shown as a tree.

steps.title: Keep what you found
steps.text: ViWo already saves every flow as it comes, next to the workspace's other runtime output (.runtime/mitmproxy-gui/<target>/flows.mitm). To keep a selection, use File, Save in mitmproxy. Open a saved file later with File, Open.
steps.expect: A .mitm file you can open again in mitmproxy.
